domain: Civil hydrographic charting and aids-to-navigation administration - Notice to Mariners correction cycles, light lists and sailing directions, station identity and characteristic, source diagrams and zones of confidence, sector arcs, and reporting of extinguished or off-station aids
axioms: An identity is held by many independent documents at once; a name is changed only when every holder of it has been enumerated, and corrected in an order that never leaves a holder navigating on a name that resolves to nothing.
Corrections are numbered and applied in sequence; a folio missing one correction looks fully corrected to its holder, so agreement can never be assumed from appearance.
A light exhibited before its notice is promulgated is more dangerous than no light: the world sees a name the documents do not yet carry.
Every sounding carries its survey date and confidence; a dated claim is a claim about the past and must be re-surveyed before anything is built on it.
An unattended aid fails silently; the design question is never whether it works but who learns that it stopped, by what means, and how long after.
A chart is published to everyone who holds one, permanently - whatever is placed on it is public and cannot be recalled.
The arc over which a light is visible is a deliberate decision; a station seen from outside its intended sector is a defect even when the light itself is correct.
primitives: holder of the identity (plugin.json mcpServers key, marketplace row, settings.json on each machine, plugin cache dir, npm registry entry, GitHub repo name and redirect, interflux and Clavain references)
correction and its sequence number (a commit, push, pull, rename or install step, and its position relative to the others)
folio state (what one machine or one fresh session actually holds right now)
unattended aid (the 04:30 harvest timer, the explorer unit, the autosync lane)
failure report path (the signal, if any, by which a stopped aid becomes known)
sector / visible range (bind address, static root, tailnet versus public, authentication)
sounding with a survey date (each 'checked 2026-09-02' claim, re-verified read-only over ssh)
divergence between folios (a state where the two machines disagree and neither can tell)
failure_mode: Indifferent to what the code means: a semantically wrong port, a broken algorithm or a mis-shaped result is invisible so long as the names propagate and the machines agree.
Over-weights exposure and unattended failure, and will call a low-traffic tailnet-only surface a serious finding on principle rather than on consequence.
Assumes many independent holders and slow correction cycles; where a change is genuinely atomic or single-holder, it manufactures propagation risk that does not exist.
Its live-survey habit anchors on current machine state, so a design flaw that is invisible today but certain after the plan runs may be dismissed as unverified.
No purchase on within-file logic, per-step executability, ambiguous prose or test design - the whole class of defects that lives inside one task.
Treats permanence as absolute and struggles to distinguish material that is genuinely sensitive from material that is merely unintended, so exposure findings can be uniformly maximal.
